title: Convert policy evaluation to worker-pool 'survey' model and remove global mutexes
creator: Elena Kim
description:
Problem: The smart routing policy evaluator is a hotspot: a single monolithic policy runtime holds a process-global mutex while evaluating per-request rules and computing fallback candidates. Under moderate traffic patterns (mixed short-chat + long-completion workloads) we observe CPU contention, lock-induced latency spikes, and cascading backpressure to the request admission path. This is responsible for recurring P99 latency regressions and one customer incident (INC-2026-014) during an autoscaling event.

Proposal: Replace the monolithic evaluator with a lightweight worker-pool (internal name: 'survey pool') that separates read-path policy scoring from write/rollout state changes. Each incoming request will snapshot a compact policy view and submit scoring tasks to the pool. The pool uses per-shard task queues (shards mapped by region+customer-tier) and lock-free ring buffers where possible. Side effects (rollouts, metrics increments, audit writes) are handled asynchronously by a single writer per region to preserve order.

Goals: reduce lock contention, stabilize P95/P99 latency under 95th traffic percentile, make policy evaluation code adoptable in private and dedicated deployments, and leave behavior unchanged for canary traffic.

Non-goals: full rewrite of the policy DSL or policy language semantics. This iteration focuses on runtime concurrency and isolation only.

Design notes: - Snapshot representation is an immutable, compact struct containing only the fields used by fast path evaluators. - Worker pool sizes are tunable per region via config; default pool is CPU_count * 1.5 with upper cap. - Backpressure is achieved by queue-length-based admission at the request router; when queues exceed threshold we fall back to a conservative default routing policy instead of blocking the request. - Audit logs and rollout mutations are committed via an append-only regional writer with controlled batching to avoid livelock.

Trade-offs: - Additional memory per request for snapshots (estimated +2-6 KB) vs large latency wins. - Slightly higher operational complexity (new pool metrics, new per-region writer), but much simpler hot path: per-request scoring is now lock-free.

Rollout plan: 1) Feature-flagged off by default; unit tests + integration tests. 2) Enable on internal canary traffic (10% of internal) for 48 hours. 3) Gradually ramp to 30% customer traffic, monitor P50/P95/P99 and failure rates for 72 hours. 4) If stable, promote to 100% and remove feature flag after 2 weeks of stable telemetry.

Observability additions: queue depth gauges, per-shard processing latency, pool utilization, writer batching stats, and a derived alert on queue-growth-rate.

Artifacts: design doc https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SE/Survey+Worker+Pool, initial PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/smart-router/pull/6789, benchmark run https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/routeperf/survey-pool-compare?orgId=1
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests cover snapshot creation, scoring semantics, and writer ordering guarantees
Benchmarks show >=25% reduction in P99 policy-eval CPU time on representative load (mixed workloads)
No semantic regressions vs baseline: routing decisions for the existing test harness match 100% for stable rulesets
Gradual rollout executed with no new customer-facing errors and stable latency for 72h at 30% traffic
New metrics (queue_depth, pool_utilization, writer_batches) present in Grafana and documented
